text:
maria: quick follow-up on the dedicated-pool autoscale RFC — small sync? wondering about the interface we expose to the rest of the control plane (admit vs execute split, plus fallbacks).

tao: +1. can we avoid the operator owning cost accounting? want the control plane to decide admission priorities, operator just executes.

jess: i worry about coupling — if cp decides admission and operator enforces, we need an idempotent lease token that can be replayed. otherwise racey.

ankit: suggested contract: admit(token) -> Lease{node_set, ttl, credit_consumed_estimate}. operator.Run(Lease) must be side-effect free on retries.

sofie: not sure we can give a good cost estimate up-front for batching workloads. estimate will be fuzzy; propose we attach a conservative upper-bound and allow operator to return actual_consumed after allocation.

dave: what about eviction ownership? if operator evicts due to thermal or infra failure, it should return a reason code and optionally a replacement intent. cp can then requeue or fallback.

maria: +++ eviction reason codes are key. also want to support a low-latency fallback path: accept->fast-path small headroom pool vs full allocation.

jess: sketch of config in case it's useful: 
```yaml
admissionApiVersion: v2
modes:
  - name: fast-path
    headroom: 2  # slots to keep warm (soft)
  - name: full-alloc
    prewarm: true
    maxTTL: 5m
```

tao: UX question — how will product teams express latency vs cost preferences? per-tenant SLO weight? a simple enum (latency|balanced|cost) would be easier to adopt.

ankit: agree enum is fine initially. autoscaler then maps enum->budgeted-headroom tokens and admission priority. we can evolve to numeric budgets later.

sofie: observability: we must surface admit decision trace: why rejected, which pool, estimated vs actual tokens. otherwise debugging will be impossible.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: autoscaler/1.4 -> staging at 11:23 UTC :rocket:

maria: next steps i propose: (1) define admit token schema (idempotent + ttl + preference enum), (2) add eviction reason codes, (3) instrument admit->execute trace events. volunteers?

jess: i can draft token schema and idempotency rules.

ankit: i'll do eviction reason taxonomy and operator return contract.

tao: i'll own observability trace/events and a quick mapping from preference enum->headroom policy.

maria: thanks — posting RFC follow-up with owners. meeting only if complex blockers surface. :thumbsup:
